description: This classic New England Clam Chowder is a creamy, hearty delight, perfect for chilly evenings. Packed with tender clams, potatoes, and savory bacon, it is a comforting bowl of pure American tradition. Its rich, velvety texture and deep flavors make it an unforgettable culinary experience.

instructions.title: Cook the Bacon
instructions.text: In a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, cook the diced bacon over medium heat until crispy. Remove the bacon with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving about 2 tablespoons of bacon fat in the pot.

instructions.title: Saute Aromatics
instructions.text: Add the butter to the pot with the bacon fat. Once melted, add the diced onion and celery. Cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Do not brown them.

instructions.title: Make the Roux
instructions.text: Sprinkle the flour over the softened vegetables and stir constantly for 1-2 minutes. This creates a roux that will thicken the chowder. Make sure there are no lumps.

instructions.title: Add Liquids and Potatoes
instructions.text: Gradually whisk in the clam juice and water until smooth. Add the diced potatoes to the pot. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce the heat to low, cover, and cook until the potatoes are tender, about 10-15 minutes.

instructions.title: Incorporate Cream and Clams
instructions.text: Once the potatoes are tender, stir in the heavy cream and whole milk. Add the drained chopped clams to the pot. Heat gently, stirring frequently, until the chowder is hot throughout. Do not let it boil after adding cream, as it can curdle.

instructions.title: Season and Serve
instructions.text: Season the chowder with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste. Ladle the hot chowder into bowls, garnish with the reserved crispy bacon and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately, perhaps with oyster crackers or crusty bread.

tips: Do not overcook the clams, especially if using fresh ones. They become rubbery quickly. Add them towards the end of cooking, just enough to heat through.
For extra flavor, use a good quality smoked bacon. You can also substitute some of the water with fish or chicken broth for a richer base.

Chowder thickens as it cools. If reheating, you might need to add a splash of milk or cream to achieve the desired consistency. Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days.
